title: Increasing Redevelopment Projects in South Mumbai and their Effect on Real Estate Supply, Prices, and Traffic Congestion

detail.title: Increasing Redevelopment Projects in South Mumbai and their Effect on Real Estate Supply, Prices, and Traffic Congestion
detail.abstract: Redevelopment of ageing housing stock has emerged as the principal strategy to unlock scarce land and meet housing demand in Mumbai. This paper investigates the recent surge in redevelopment projects in South Mumbai (often referred to as South Bombay), and evaluates their effects on three outcomes: the effective supply of real estate, property prices, and local traffic congestion. The study combines a purposive household survey of local residents and commuters, secondary market reports by major real estate consultancies, and recent news and policy material. Findings indicate redevelopment contributes new housing units and upgrades infrastructure but does not uniformly increase affordable supply in South Mumbai because large parts of the area are heritage or physically constrained. Redevelopment also exerts upward pressure on local rents and sale prices through scarcity, amenity upgrade and temporary displacement-induced demand; meanwhile construction activity and higher dwelling densities increase traffic pressures short term, although planned infrastructure projects may ease congestion medium term. The paper concludes with targeted policy recommendations for balancing redevelopment, affordability and local mobility.

title: Information Before Action: A Fiscal-Epistemic Framework for Institutional and Interdisciplinary Analysis

detail.title: Information Before Action: A Fiscal-Epistemic Framework for Institutional and Interdisciplinary Analysis
detail.abstract: This paper argues that interdisciplinary analysis presupposes an often-unspoken condition: a differentiated account of information flows. Without specifying how information is admitted, processed, and closed within institutional systems, cross-domain inquiry remains largely interpretive—capable of explaining meaning and representation, yet unable to reach the level of execution where rules become decisions and decisions become recordable outcomes. Building on Edward Said’s insight that narrative organizes social space, the paper introduces a parallel, non-narrative layer of institutional operation: fiscal-administrative information as an execution grammar. Here, information is not treated as communication or discourse, but as legally accountable and procedurally admissible material capable of triggering decision nodes and producing administrative closure. This distinction clarifies why narrative analysis can reveal how power is articulated and normalized, while leaving under-specified how power is implemented through routine verification, eligibility gates, documentation demands, and record making practices. The paper advances an evidence discipline centered on admissibility and traceability, showing how institutional strain becomes observable as friction within closure processes—manifesting as delays, churn, exceptions, and misalignments between policy design and operational reality— without requiring prior agreement on moral or political attribution. The contribution is not a replacement for social science or critical theory, but an interface: a minimal grammar for translating interdisciplinary questions into institutionally processable evidence, enabling consistent cross-domain analysis across taxation, education finance, and credentialing systems.

title: Towards Sustainable Productivity Innovation: Development Level, Regional Disparities, and Spatio-Temporal Dynamics of China's New Quality Productive Forces

detail.title: Towards Sustainable Productivity Innovation: Development Level, Regional Disparities, and Spatio-Temporal Dynamics of China's New Quality Productive Forces
detail.abstract: New Quality Productive Forces (NQPF), defined as innovation-driven green productivity, guide productivity innovation and sustainable development, serving as crucial drivers for high-quality economic growth in China. This paper evaluates the advancement of NQPF across 30 Chinese provinces from 2014 to 2022, exploring regional disparities and spatiotemporal evolution patterns. We developed a comprehensive indicator system that integrates innovation-driven development, technological innovation, industrial optimization, and sustainable practices. Analytical techniques such as the entropy method, Dagum Gini coefficient, Moran's I index, and kernel density estimation were utilized. Findings indicate a general upward trend in NQPF development nationwide; however, significant regional imbalances remain, with the eastern provinces leading, followed by the central and northeastern regions, while the western provinces lag, thereby widening regional disparities. Spatial correlation analysis reveals a positive spatial association of NQPF, with higher concentrations in the east and lower concentrations in the west and northeast. Based on these findings, the following policy recommendations are proposed: First, promote regional integration and foster coordinated cooperation among the eastern, central, and western regions, while formulating differentiated policies tailored to regional characteristics. Second, implement an innovation-driven strategy and increase investment in R&D. Third, drive industrial upgrading and optimize industry to ensure high-quality development.

detail.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic prompted global restrictions on mass gatherings, yet the causal effect of large religious congregations on disease spread remains understudied and difficult to isolate. This study leverages a unique natural experiment from Pakistan, which, contrary to other Muslim nations, reopened mosques for congregational prayers for Ramadan in 2020 during a critical phase of the pandemic. We apply the synthetic control method to estimate the impact of this policy, constructing a counterfactual for Pakistan using countries that enforced mosque closures. We find that the reopening led to a significant increase in COVID-19 transmission, causing an estimated 5,600 additional cases and approximately 112 excess fatalities over 21 days after mosque reopening, representing a substantial portion of the national case load during this phase. These results provide robust, quasi-experimental evidence on the public health costs of exempting religious gatherings from public health mandates. Conclusions about causality can be made, although with caution, given the natural experiment setup, highlighting the critical need to manage the epidemiological risks of mass gatherings during a health crisis.

detail.abstract: As the global internet infrastructure grows in complexity, traditional routing protocols face limitations in adapting to real-time network conditions, particularly in the context of dynamic path prediction, network failures, and congestion. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), a type of machine learning model, have shown great promise in learning optimal routing paths by representing networks as graphs, where nodes are network devices, and edges represent communication links. This paper explores the application of GNNs for resilient internet routing, particularly focusing on their ability to predict optimal paths in real-time, enhancing network robustness and traffic engineering. By using GNNs to model inter-domain and intradomain routing, the study aims to demonstrate how machine learning can improve the adaptability, reliability, and efficiency of routing protocols. Experimental results show that GNN-based routing significantly enhances path prediction accuracy, reduces network congestion, and improves network resilience in the face of link failures and changing traffic patterns.

title: Fiscal Geometry for Global Capital Markets: Rendering Cross-Border Tax, Audit, and Valuation Gates on the X-Y Plane

detail.title: Fiscal Geometry for Global Capital Markets: Rendering Cross-Border Tax, Audit, and Valuation Gates on the X-Y Plane
detail.abstract: This working paper positions global capital markets as an interface domain in which long accumulated financial events—distributed across firms, structures, and time—are compressed into tradable, auditable, and taxable states. Rather than reconstructing historical datasets, it treats “history” as an event aggregate that becomes observable only when routed through institutional gates that force classification, verification, and settlement. Using Fiscal Geometry (FG) as a rendering grammar on a fixed X–Y plane, the paper formalizes how cross-border fiscal reclassification (X: Cross-Border Fiscal Shift) and post-tax succession capacity (Y: Intergenerational Post-Tax Capacity) jointly shape the visibility, density, and deformation of global institutional capital flows at market-facing interfaces. The paper integrates three unavoidable gate families that condition the feasibility of non-personal capital movement across jurisdictions: (i) valuation and pricing as market frames that compress dispersed event histories into realizable value states; (ii) audit and verification as evidence gates that standardize informational granularity and produce settlement-ready representations; and (iii) international tax law, including treaty networks, anti-abuse provisions, and outbound inclusion architectures, as jurisdictional filters that reshape feasible cross-border pathways without altering the underlying economic event aggregate. A controlled rendering demonstration—holding institutional capital paths constant while varying gate configurations—illustrates how different treaty and outbound inclusion structures generate distinct path densities, bottlenecks, and shadow regions on the same X–Y grammar. The analysis is descriptive and non-normative, offering a methodological framework for observing how global capital mobility is structured by interacting institutional gates rather than by intent-driven behavior or policy optimization.

detail.abstract:
Recent inflation episodes have exposed growing limitations in the transmission of interest rate policy, particularly in economies characterised by high asset wealth, accumulated savings, and reduced marginal borrowing sensitivity. This paper introduces the National Economic Stabilisation Repository (NESR), a proposed complementary stabilisation framework designed to temporarily restrain household liquidity during inflationary periods while preserving full private ownership of funds.
NESR operates by diverting a calibrated portion of pre-tax income above defined thresholds into individual, restricted-access accounts held within the banking system. These balances are not spendable during activation periods but are fully released once macroeconomic conditions normalise. Interest generated on restricted balances is pooled temporarily and returned to individuals through tax offsets or credits to avoid reinforcing inflationary pressures.
The framework is rules-based, reversible, and compatible with existing tax, payroll, and banking systems. NESR is presented as a supplementary policy instrument intended to reduce over-reliance on interest rate adjustments and to distribute demand restraint more evenly across households. This paper outlines the conceptual rationale, design principles, institutional pathways, and limitations of NESR, and identifies areas requiring further modelling and pilot testing.

title: Comperative Analysis of the Role of Confessional Statement in the Nigerian and Indian Criminal Justice System

detail.title: Comperative Analysis of the Role of Confessional Statement in the Nigerian and Indian Criminal Justice System
detail.abstract: Confessions constitute one of the most potent forms of evidence in criminal adjudication, yet their probative value remains deeply contested across jurisdictions. This study undertakes a comparative analysis of the role of confessions under the Nigerian and Indian criminal justice systems, examining the legal framework governing confessional statements, the constitutional safeguards designed to secure voluntariness, and the judicial interpretation of confessional admissibility. While both jurisdictions inherited English evidentiary principles, their contemporary approaches reveal points of convergence and contrast. In Nigeria, the Evidence Act 2011 and constitutional guarantees under sections 35 and 36 of the 1999 Constitution regulate confessional admissibility, with jurisprudence emphasizing the voluntariness of statements as a prerequisite. Similarly, the Indian Evidence Act 1872, supplemented by judicial activism shaped by fundamental rights under Articles 20 and 21 of the Indian Constitution, underscores concerns over coercion and reliability. Scholarly critiques reveal a persistent gap between law and practice in both systems, particularly in the context of custodial interrogations, police torture, and plea based confessional arrangements. In this regard, the insights of Ashiru on comparative criminal procedure and judicial oversight in plea agreements illuminate broader themes relating to judicial discretion and procedural fairness. Using doctrinal, comparative and qualitative methods, this research interrogates legal texts, case law, academic commentary, and empirical findings to assess whether existing safeguards adequately protect accused persons. The study concludes by identifying weaknesses in enforcement mechanisms and recommending reforms aimed at strengthening human rights compliance, evidentiary reliability, and judicial accountability within both jurisdictions.

detail.title: "Immer noch Sturm"? Über Geschichte(n), Dialog, Recht und Vielfalt (“Still stormy”? On history, stories, dialogue, law, and diversity)
detail.abstract:
German Abstract:Das Werk untersucht interdisziplinär die Wirkung historischer Narrative auf Identität, Recht und Verständigung in der Alpen-Adria-Region. Im Mittelpunkt steht die Frage, wie erzählte Geschichte kollektive Selbstbilder prägt, politische Ansprüche legitimiert und Versöhnung ermöglicht. Am Beispiel des Kärntner Minderheitenkonflikts wird das Spannungsverhältnis zwischen juristischer Durchsetzung von Minderheitenrechten und dialogischerKonfliktbearbeitung analysiert. Aufbauend auf Dialoginitiativen zwischen slowenischen und deutschsprachigen Organisationen wird deutlich, wie Recht und Dialog sich im Prozess der Anerkennung ergänzen. Persönliche Erfahrungen werden dabei mit Ansätzen der Friedensforschung, insbesondere Kelmans Problem Solving Workshops, verbunden. Recht und Dialog erscheinen als komplementäre Instrumente gesellschaftlicher Transformation: Recht schafft Schutz und Verbindlichkeit, Dialog fördert Verständigung und Anerkennung. Im Konzept der „offenen Identität“ – einer Identität ohne Feindbild – entwirft Pirker eine Perspektive auf Pluralität, Anerkennung und gemeinsame Verantwortung. So wirddie Alpen-Adria-Region zu einem Labor für Geschichte, Vielfalt und europäische Erinnerungskultur.


English Abstract: This work takes an interdisciplinary approach to examining the impact of historical narratives on identity, law and understanding in the Alps-Adriatic region. It focuses on the question of how narrated history shapes collective self-images, legitimises political claims and enables reconciliation. Using the example of the Carinthian minority conflict, it analyses the tension between the legal enforcement of minority rights and dialogue-based conflict resolution. Building on dialogue initiatives between Slovenian and German-speaking organisations, it highlights how law and dialogue complement each other in the process of recognition. Personal experiences are combined with approaches from peace research, in particular Kelman's problem-solving workshops. Law and dialogue appear to be complementary instruments of social transformation: law creates protection and binding commitments, while dialogue promotes understanding and recognition. In the concept of ‘open identity’ – an identity without an enemy image – Pirker develops a perspective on plurality, recognition and shared responsibility. In this way, the Alps-Adriatic region becomes a laboratory for history, diversity and European culture of remembrance.

detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is widely promoted as a solution to mental healthcare access and cost issues. Supporters claim AI chatbots, from Woebot to ChatGPT and Replika, can democratize care with round-the-clock support in underserved places. Yet, examining the technology, clinical evidence, and ethics shows major concerns. Today's mental health AI is fragmented, lacks solid clinical validation, and can fail, sometimes with serious consequences. This report reviews flaws in today's mental health AI, focusing on consumer-facing conversational agents marketed or used for mental health support, not clinician-deployed diagnostic tools. Research, legal cases, and clinical studies reveal these failures stem from a mismatch between machine learning's probabilistic methods and the strict safety needed in psychiatry. The analysis details the "Conversational AI Tax", the burden on vulnerable users, and exposes the "Wellness Loophole," letting unverified algorithms avoid regulation. The report addresses the "validation trap" in LLMs, models built to agree with users, which risks harm for those with suicidal or psychotic symptoms. Cases like NEDA's "Tessa" and Character.AI failures show urgent need for reform. Mental health AI must advance beyond generative chatbots to neurosymbolic, hybrid, and clinically validated methods. This paper serves as a critical foundation for developing safer, more effective mental health AI systems that can genuinely support vulnerable individuals while avoiding the pitfalls of current approaches.

title: Born Out-Of-Season: Talent Allocation and Economic Conditions

detail.title: Born Out-Of-Season: Talent Allocation and Economic Conditions
detail.abstract: This paper studies how regional economic conditions, birth timing, and institutional rules shape talent allocation into high-risk/high-reward payoff structure occupations. Using rich data on English-born professional footballers and exploiting exogenous variation from European Structural Funds in the United Kingdom (1990-2000), we show that improved local conditions reduced the share of summer-born children, who are disadvantaged by age-based cutoffs in youth academies but exhibit higher underlying talent. Although regional income per capita did not significantly change, fertility timing shifted, shrinking this high-potential group: players born after the intervention exhibit lower peak market values, reflecting how economic and institutional factors can misallocate talent.

title: The Decimal-Percentile Tax - A Novel and Structural Overhaul of Existing Tax Systems

detail.title: The Decimal-Percentile Tax - A Novel and Structural Overhaul of Existing Tax Systems
detail.abstract:
This paper proposes the wholesale abolition of personal and corporate income taxes, capital-gains taxes, net-wealth taxes, inheritance taxes, and the current general goods-and-services tax (GST/VAT) in favour of two interlocking, proportional mechanisms that both empower and restrict the government to impose no tax burden greater or lesser than the “fair share” upon the individual taxpayer.

  1. The Specific Spending Tax: a hierarchical, infinitely extensible decimal-based classification system tracking every economically distinct good and service sold in the economy, with each terminal node carrying its own rate. Rates are adjusted by regulation (not legislation) and are strictly required to reflect quantifiable fiscal externalities or internalised fiscal benefits measured in dollars to the public budget or GDP. Moral, distributional, or public-health arguments unrelated to fiscal cost are expressly prohibited as primary justifications.

  2. A Personal Percentile Charge: every inbound transfer to a natural person (salary, bonus, dividend, interest, gift, inheritance, gambling win, crypto-to-fiat conversion, loan drawdown used for consumption, etc.) is subject to an annual levy whose maximum permissible rate equals the recipient’s exact income percentile rank in the previous tax year, capped at 49 % for the 99th percentile and above, and 0 % at or below the median. The effect is a continuous, bracket-free, rank-based progressive levy with an explicit moral ceiling: the citizen must at all times be given the privilege of the “lion’s share,” as it were, of their earnings.

Preliminary calibrations using 2023–24 New Zealand tax and income-distribution data suggest the proposal is strongly revenue-positive relative to the current system; even after fully exempting the bottom half of earners and applying a top rate below the current highest marginal rate, because the base becomes near-impossible to avoid once realisation and trust loopholes are eliminated.

title: From Stability to Persistence, to Interconnection: The Evolution of Aggregate Unemployment Theories Through a Bibliometric Lens

detail.title: From Stability to Persistence, to Interconnection: The Evolution of Aggregate Unemployment Theories Through a Bibliometric Lens
detail.abstract: This article provides a systematic bibliometric analysis of the theoretical evolution in labor market equilibrium research from 1998 to 2024, charting the development of the Non-Accelerating Inflation Rate of Unemployment (NAIRU), the Hysteresis Hypothesis (HH), and the emerging Chain Reaction Theory (CRT). By analyzing 350 publications from Web of Science and Scopus using co-authorship, co-word, citation, and thematic clustering techniques, this study maps the intellectual structure and historical trajectory of the field. Our findings reveal a definitive paradigm shift from static equilibrium models toward dynamic frameworks. Crucially, the analysis identifies a significant dialectical relationship between NAIRU and HH, evidenced by a strong positive correlation their publication volumes, indicating they developed through scholarly contestation. This dynamic ultimately fostered the conditions for CRT's emergence as a third, integrative analytical pillar. The bibliometric evidence confirms CRT's consolidation by addressing key limitations of its predecessors, reframing unemployment as the outcome of a dynamic system characterized by interdependencies, lagged adjustments, and spillover effects. The study further documents a corresponding methodological progression from basic econometric tests to sophisticated multi-equation systems. Emerging research fronts are identified, emphasizing supply shock analysis, machine learning applications, and labor resilience policies. We conclude that CRT represents the most promising synthesizing framework for contemporary labor market analysis, offering a nuanced toolkit for understanding unemployment dynamics in an era of interconnected economic disruptions.

detail.abstract: Early warning systems (EWS) and community preparedness are central to climate adaptation, yet there is limited causal evidence on their effectiveness. We report interim results from a randomized controlled trial of a combined Community-Based Early Warning System (CBEWS) and Community-Based Climate Risk Management (CBCRM) program in Georgia. Using baseline data and a phone survey data, we estimate short-run impacts on warning receipt, protective actions, and household welfare. We find no significant effects on receiving early warnings, warning lead time, or clarity. Behavioral responses also show limited changes, aside from a modest increase in livestock protection. Consistent with this, we detect no impacts on damages, food-related coping, or expenditures. These muted effects likely reflect mild hazard intensity, partial implementation exposure, and slow-moving nature of preparedness behaviors. The study contributes experimental evidence on community-based disaster preparedness and highlights challenges in achieving short-term impacts.

title: Research on the Contagious Characteristics of Digital Financial Risks: A Perspective Based on Blockchain

detail.title: Research on the Contagious Characteristics of Digital Financial Risks: A Perspective Based on Blockchain
detail.abstract:
With the continuous development of the digital finance industry, increasing attention has been paid to digital financial risks. From a technological perspective, the digital finance industry can be divided into artificial intelligence digital finance, blockchain digital finance, and cloud computing digital finance. Among them, blockchain digital finance represented by digital currencies has the strongest speculative risk, and there is potential for systemic contagion risk, resulting in risk spillover effects. Therefore, this study is based on reality, using theoretical analysis and empirical model methods to quantitatively measure the diffusion effects of blockchain digital finance risks and the regional disparities of this effect, aiming to provide positive guidance for future investors and policymakers in the new financial industry.

This study extensively employs case studies and theoretical analysis to derive the characteristics of diffusion effects theoretically in the digital currency market, as well as the differences in this effect under different circumstances. Based on this, corresponding conjectures and hypotheses are proposed. In the empirical section, this paper focuses on verifying the rationality of the aforementioned conjectures and hypotheses. Market price volatility is utilized as a measure of market risk. Using daily and monthly data from global financial markets, real estate markets, and digital currency markets from 2008 to 2024, this study empirically investigates the risk diffusion effects of the digital currency market on traditional financial markets and real estate markets using the DY spillover index model. The research findings indicate that there are bidirectional spillover effects between the digital currency market and traditional financial markets as well as real estate markets, and there are regional disparities. Within the digital currency market, Ethereum (ETH) emerges as the cryptocurrency with the most significant net spillover effect, exerting the strongest risk diffusion effect on other digital currencies. Regarding the risk diffusion effects of digital currencies on global traditional financial markets, empirical results demonstrate that digital currency assets exhibit a considerable risk diffusion effect between institutional investors and the U.S. stock market, surpassing that with the Chinese stock market. Concerning the risk diffusion effects of digital currencies on the real estate markets of major financial centers worldwide, the study reveals that the digital currency market exerts the strongest risk diffusion effect on the real estate market in Hong Kong, surpassing other markets. Following the empirical findings of the paper, this study completes a closed loop from conjectures and hypotheses based on theoretical analysis to real-world market data, organically linking financial theory with societal reality. Based on the aforementioned research conclusions, it is recommended that digital currency investors and regulators of digital financial risks continuously track blockchain technological innovations and fully understand the behaviors of blockchain investors to optimize regulatory policies subsequently, thereby better mitigating the diffusion and spillover effects of blockchain financial risks.

detail.abstract: We develop a novel bank-level index of fintech integration by mitigating media bias in index construction. We then explore its relationship with bank stability across 56 economies from 2010 to 2022. We uncover a U-shaped relationship between this index and bank stability. Initially, fintech increases bank fragility, but as integration deepens, it ultimately enhances stability. Interestingly, this pattern is influenced by both bank-level and industry-level factors. Strong, foreign-owned banks experience a milder initial decline in stability, reflecting their ability to navigate the fintech landscape effectively. Furthermore, banks operating in developed, competitive markets show a flatter relationship, emphasizing the importance of a supportive ecosystem. The role of regulatory sandboxes varies depending on factors such as bank competition, economic growth, regulatory strength, financial development, and access to credit information. We further validate our findings using an instrumental variables approach and an alternative index of fintech integration, reinforcing the robustness of the identified U-shaped relationship between fintech and bank stability.

title:
Gross Domestic Human Progress (GDHP)
A Beyond GDP Framework for Measuring Human Development in the Age of AI

detail.title:
Gross Domestic Human Progress (GDHP)
A Beyond GDP Framework for Measuring Human Development in the Age of AI
detail.abstract:
Gross Domestic Product (GDP) remains the dominant measure of national economic performance, yet its limitations in capturing human well-being, institutional quality, and long-term sustainability are increasingly evident. While these gaps have motivated a broad Beyond-GDP literature, the rapid advance of artificial intelligence (AI) introduces a more urgent challenge. In AI-augmented economies, economic output can expand even as human participation, agency, and perceived opportunity stagnate or decline, weakening the traditional link between growth and human progress.

This paper proposes Gross Domestic Human Progress (GDHP) as a complementary framework that preserves GDP as a measure of economic scale while adjusting it by a Development Resilience Factor (DRF). DRF captures the human, institutional, and psychological conditions under which economic activity is generated and sustained. Drawing on research in subjective well-being and hope, particularly the work of Carol Graham, the framework treats mental well-being, hope, trust, and institutional legitimacy as leading indicators of human resilience and development stress. GDHP, defined as GDP multiplied by DRF, distinguishes automation-driven growth from growth that produces durable human progress and outlines an exploratory extension—the Human Development Spread (HDS)—for potential application in sovereign risk assessment.

title: ROE Premiums: An Equilibrium Outcome of Regulatory Bargaining with Cost Uncertainty

detail.title: ROE Premiums: An Equilibrium Outcome of Regulatory Bargaining with Cost Uncertainty

declarations.declarationOfInterest: In addition to being an MBA candidate at the University of Michigan, I am also employed by a regulated energy utility company.

detail.abstract: Utility regulators frequently authorize returns on equity that exceed utilities’ costs of capital. Existing theories attribute ROE premiums to capture, regulatory holdup, gradualism, or static cooperative bargaining. In contrast, this paper demonstrates that ROE premiums emerge endogenously when rate cases are modeled as repeated bargaining between utilities and regulators under private cost information. Using a Rubinstein bargaining framework with asymmetric information, the model characterizes a cutoff belief that governs when regulators optimally screen versus pool utility cost types. The analysis yields sharp comparative statics linking patience, potential cost padding, and project benefits to the regulator’s screening or pooling strategy. These results provide an integrated explanation for persistent ROE premiums and generate testable implications for regulatory policy and utility strategy.

title: The Gold Channel: How Regional Gold Saving Behavior Shapes House Price Dynamics in Türkiye
affiliations: Government of the Republic of Turkey - Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey and

detail.title: The Gold Channel: How Regional Gold Saving Behavior Shapes House Price Dynamics in Türkiye
detail.abstract: Households in many emerging economies hold substantial alternative assets such as gold and cryptocurrencies, yet macro effects from these assets are difficult to explore due to measurement challenges. Exploiting Türkiye's cross-provincial heterogeneity in gold saving and the exogenous 2023-2024 global gold rally, we study how gold wealth transmits to housing market. Using a province-level administrative dataset within a novel approach to proxy the formal and informal gold tendency and a difference-in-differences (DID) design, we show that house prices rise significantly more in high-gold provinces, with an average 10% cumulative additional price increase due to the wealth effects from gold. Mechanism tests indicate a liquidity channel: the cash-purchase share increases, while credit-financed transactions do not. At the same time, secondary market sales fall, consistent with strengthened homeowner balance sheets tightening resale supply. A Bartik-style instrumental variable (IV) strategy based on passive gains supports causality. The findings highlight that alternative saving instruments can fuel real asset inflation through cash, suggesting that monetary and macroprudential policy frameworks focused solely on credit flows may miss important pressures in inflationary environments.

detail.title: Investor Trading Behavior and Intermediate Prospect Theory Value in Cross-sectional Expected Returns
detail.abstract: This study demonstrates that investor trading behavior influences the positive relationship between past intermediate prospect theory value (PTV) based on 12-month return distributions and expected returns. The predictive power of intermediate PTV portfolios is mainly driven by individual investors' high trading activity, with foreign investors also contributing to it. Their effect arises from the opposite position: individuals show net selling (buying) in a high (low) PTV portfolio, whereas foreigners do the reverse. These patterns suggest that foreign investors' trades align with the PTV's predictive signals, unlike those of individuals. These findings offer behavioral insights into return predictability and provide a foundation for future investor-focused research.

title: When Cyber Risk Hits the Headlines: Media Salience and Market Reactions
affiliations: , Northern Kentucky University, Providence College - School of Business, Shanghai Lixin University of Accounting and Finance and Old Dominion University

detail.title: When Cyber Risk Hits the Headlines: Media Salience and Market Reactions
detail.abstract: This study investigates how media salience influences investor reactions to cybercrime incidents and the moderating role of corporate social responsibility (CSR). Drawing on salience theory, we hypothesize that salient news coverage amplifies immediate market responses and induces subsequent reversals. Using a sample of 1,310 cyberattacks on U.S. listed firms from 2005–2019, combined with MarketPsych cybercrime headline news and ESG data, we find that higher salience significantly exacerbates short-term stock price declines and abnormal volatility, followed by a partial post-event correction. Further analysis reveals that firms with stronger CSR performance experience attenuated negative reactions and volatility, underscoring CSR’s role as reputational insurance. Robustness checks, including endogeneity controls, alternative salience measures, and expanded event types, confirm these findings. Our results contribute to behavioral finance, risk management, and CSR literature by highlighting the interplay between media salience, investor behavior, and corporate resilience in the context of rising cyber risk.
